name: Lyo.Json
tagline: The Lyo HTTP JSON contract and typed JSON parse and export.
description:
The JSON contract Lyo APIs, clients, and message-queue envelopes serialize against lives in Lyo.Json: camelCase properties, case-insensitive reads, nulls omitted on write, camelCase string enums, and ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles so EF-shaped graphs serialize.

JsonService.Default is that contract. Pass a JsonOptions instance or new JsonService(o => { ... }) to change naming, enums, number handling, write omission, encoding, and comments. Pass a JsonSerializerOptions instance and it is copied and used as-is. One instance is safe for concurrent parse and export. Options are fixed after construction.

Byte methods take an optional Encoding. A missing argument uses the service encoding (UTF-8 without a BOM). A character span is already decoded. File and stream reads detect a BOM. Async twins and NDJSON streaming exist on net10.0.

Converters under JsonConverters/ stay unregistered until UseStringScalarConverters is set. Add them for one integration through LyoJsonSerializerOptionsBuilder. Namespaces match the package: options are Lyo.Json.LyoJsonSerializerOptions and converters live in Lyo.Json.JsonConverters.
features: JsonService.Default, new JsonService(JsonOptions), new JsonService(configure), or new JsonService(JsonSerializerOptions) for camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, or PascalCase, string or numeric enums, and write omission of nulls, defaults, empty strings, and empty collections.
`Order` is Defined (declaration order), Alphabetical, or Specified. Specified uses `[MemberOrder]` and `OrderNames`. Defined does not sort.
`ExportFormattedToJsonString` writes formatter fields in dictionary order. `ExportColumnsToJsonString` writes a header-to-property map in that same order. `Order` does not reorder either list.
Optional Encoding on ParseBytes, Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte>), ExportToJsonBytes, and TryExport. UTF-8 uses the System.Text.Json span APIs.
NDJSON: ParseNdjsonFile, ParseNdjsonStream, ParseNdjsonString, and ParseNdjsonBytes, plus net10 IAsyncEnumerable for file and stream. Export writes one compact value per line.
LyoJsonSerializerOptions.Create, Create(configure), and ApplyTo for the HTTP contract. LyoJsonSerializerOptionsBuilder adds converters.
A top-level JSON array binds List<T> or T[].
JsonNodeGraph converts a JsonNode to dictionaries, lists, and scalars so YAML, XML, and TOML share this contract.
ObjectJsonConverter and the string scalar converters stay opt-in.

`ExportToJsonStringFromDataTable` writes a data table as a JSON array of objects. `ParseStringAsDataTable` reads it back. `hasFooterRow` moves the last object into the footer. Cell text stays text, including empty strings and a leading zero.

sections.title: ASP.NET export
sections.text: When an ASP.NET JsonOptions instance is registered, construct new JsonService(serializerOptions: aspNetSerializerOptions). The service copies those options and does not apply JsonOptions on top, and it does not mutate the host instance. ConfigureHttpJsonOptions can copy the same defaults with LyoJsonSerializerOptions.ApplyTo.

sections.title: Why record converters live in metadata
sections.text: SocialPlatformInfoJsonConverter and LanguageCodeInfoJsonConverter resolve a code to a registry record, so they stay in Lyo.Common.Metadata. A project that only wants the scalar converters does not acquire the catalogs.
